# AI Phone Receptionist

URL: https://www.vargersoft.com/ai/ai-receptionist/
Price: Setup: $1,950 one time; Monthly service: $349 per month

A phone line that always answers, in the language your caller speaks.

A missed call is usually a customer who calls the next business on the list. Most small businesses miss calls at lunch, after hours and whenever the counter is busy. And when the caller speaks Spanish and nobody on shift does, the call ends in thirty seconds.

Answers every call, day or night, with a natural human-sounding voice.

Detects whether the caller speaks English or Spanish and answers in that language.

Books, confirms and reschedules appointments on your calendar.

Answers common questions: hours, location, services, prices you approve.

Transfers to a person when the caller asks or the situation needs it.

Emails you a written summary of every call.

A new phone number, or your current number forwarded to the agent.

Your choice of voice and a bilingual script written around your business.

Calendar connection and call-transfer rules.

500 minutes of calls every month. Extra minutes at $0.35.

Monthly review of call summaries and script adjustments.

Q: Will callers know they are talking to an AI?
A: Yes. The agent says it is a virtual assistant at the start of the call. It sounds natural, but we do not present it as a person.

Q: Can I keep my current phone number?
A: Yes. You forward your number to the agent, either always or only when you do not pick up.

Q: What happens when the agent cannot answer a question?
A: It takes the message, tells the caller when to expect a call back and emails you the details. It does not make up an answer.

Q: How long does setup take?
A: Seven business days from the day we receive your business information and calendar access.

# How much does an AI chatbot for a website cost in 2026?

URL: https://www.vargersoft.com/resources/website-ai-chatbot-cost/

An AI chatbot for a business website usually costs a setup fee plus a monthly fee. Do-it-yourself tools start around $20 to $100 a month but you build and train them yourself. A done-for-you bilingual assistant from VARGERSOFT costs $850 to set up and $179 a month, and it answers, captures leads and books appointments in English and Spanish.

What drives the price

Three things set the cost: how much of your information the chatbot must learn, whether it only answers or also takes actions like booking and quoting, and how many conversations it handles each month. A chatbot that answers ten questions costs far less than one that books jobs into your calendar.

The hidden cost of "cheap"

A low monthly price often means you do the setup, write every answer and fix it when it gets something wrong. Count your own hours. If the chatbot never gets trained well, visitors still leave without an answer.

How to know it pays for itself

Take your average sale and your close rate. If one extra customer a month covers the monthly fee, the chatbot pays for itself. A shop with a $400 average job needs one new job a month to cover $179.

Questions to ask before you buy

Does it answer only from my approved information?

Does it work in Spanish natively, not by machine translation?

Can it book appointments and send me the lead right away?

Is it month to month, and do I own the conversations?

# How much does an AI receptionist cost for a small business?

URL: https://www.vargersoft.com/resources/ai-receptionist-cost-small-business/

An AI receptionist is usually paid in two parts: a one-time setup fee and a monthly fee that includes a block of call minutes. At VARGERSOFT the AI Phone Receptionist costs $1,950 to set up and $349 a month with 500 minutes included, and $0.35 for each extra minute.

What the setup fee pays for

Setup is the work of making the agent yours: writing the script around your services and prices, choosing the voice, connecting your calendar, setting the rules for when a call goes to a person, and testing it with real scenarios in both languages.

What the monthly fee pays for

The monthly fee covers the phone line, the voice and AI usage for your included minutes, the call summaries, and the monthly review where the script is adjusted from real calls.

How to estimate your minutes

Count the calls you get in a normal week and multiply by the length of a typical call. A shop with 40 calls a week at about three minutes each uses roughly 480 minutes a month. If you do not know your numbers, your phone bill or carrier portal shows them.

Questions to ask any provider

Is there a contract, or is it month to month?

What happens when I pass my included minutes?

Does it really answer in Spanish, or only read a translated script?

Who owns the call summaries and recordings?

Can it transfer to a person, and can I keep my number?

# AI receptionist vs. answering service vs. hiring: which fits?

URL: https://www.vargersoft.com/resources/ai-receptionist-vs-answering-service-vs-hiring/

An AI receptionist fits when most calls are routine: hours, prices, booking and messages. It answers at any hour in English and Spanish. A live answering service fits when callers need a person but not your person. A hired receptionist fits when the job is much more than the phone. Many businesses combine an AI receptionist with staff who take the transferred calls.

Where an AI receptionist is the wrong choice

When most calls are emotional, complex or negotiated, a person should answer. The AI is still useful after hours and for overflow, but it should not be the only voice a caller can reach.

A simple way to decide

Write down the last twenty calls and mark each one as routine or not. If fifteen or more are routine, an AI receptionist will carry most of the load and your staff keep the rest.

---

# How to answer business calls in English and Spanish without hiring

URL: https://www.vargersoft.com/resources/answer-business-calls-in-english-and-spanish/

The simplest way to answer calls in both languages without hiring is an AI receptionist that detects the caller's language and answers in it. The caller does not press a button or wait for a bilingual employee. Other options are a phone menu, a bilingual answering service, or forwarding Spanish calls to one bilingual person.

Option 1: a phone menu

"For English press 1, para español oprima 2." It is cheap and familiar. Its weakness is what happens after the button: someone still has to answer in that language.

Option 2: one bilingual employee

It works until that person is at lunch, on another call or on vacation. The business then answers in one language again.

Option 3: a bilingual answering service

A person answers and takes a message in either language. Ask whether Spanish is covered at every hour or only during certain shifts.

Option 4: an AI receptionist

The agent listens to the first words, recognizes the language and continues in it. It can book, answer questions and take messages, and it sends you the summary in the language you choose.

What to check before you choose

Call your own number after hours and see what a customer hears.

Ask a Spanish speaker to test any service with a real question.

Make sure written follow-ups, such as texts and emails, are bilingual too.

# SEO vs. AEO vs. GEO: what each one means

URL: https://www.vargersoft.com/resources/seo-vs-aeo-vs-geo/

SEO, search engine optimization, helps your pages rank in search results. AEO, answer engine optimization, shapes your content so a search engine or assistant can lift a direct answer from it. GEO, generative engine optimization, helps AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity read, trust and cite your business when they write an answer. The three share one foundation: pages a machine can read and content that answers real questions.

What should a small business do first?

Make sure each page arrives as complete HTML, with its own title and description.

Write one page per service, and answer the main question in the first two sentences.

Publish your prices, hours, service area and contact details in text, not only in images.

Add structured data for your business, services and FAQs.

Keep your name, address and phone identical everywhere they appear.

What nobody can promise

No one controls what a search engine ranks or what an AI assistant says. Honest work removes the technical reasons you are ignored and measures the result over time. Be careful with anyone who guarantees a first position or a recommendation.

---

# What is llms.txt, and does your website need it?

URL: https://www.vargersoft.com/resources/what-is-llms-txt/

llms.txt is a plain Markdown file placed at the root of a website that gives AI systems a short summary of the site and links to its most important pages. It is a proposal from 2024, not an official standard. Studies published in 2026 found that AI crawlers rarely request it, and Google has said its search products do not use it. It costs little to publish, but it will not make an unreadable website readable.

What goes inside the file

A title, a one-paragraph description of the business, and short lists of links grouped under headings such as Services, Pricing and Contact. A second file, llms-full.txt, can hold the full text of those pages.

What the evidence says

Independent studies in 2026 measured how often AI crawlers ask for the file, and the answer was almost never. One analysis reported that most sites with a valid file received no requests for it in a month. The tools that do read it today are mostly coding assistants working with developer documentation.

Should you publish one?

Yes, if it takes minutes, because a short accurate summary does no harm. Do not pay for it as if it were a ranking tool. Put the real effort into the things assistants demonstrably read: complete HTML pages, clear answers and structured data.

The file that matters more: robots.txt

robots.txt decides which crawlers may read your site at all, and the major AI crawlers follow it. A robots file that blocks them removes you from their answers, whatever your llms.txt says.

---

# What are MCP and WebMCP, in plain words?

URL: https://www.vargersoft.com/resources/what-is-mcp-and-webmcp/

MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is an open standard that lets an AI assistant connect to outside tools and data, such as a catalog, a calendar or a booking system. WebMCP is a newer proposal that lets a web page offer its own tools to an AI agent running in the visitor's browser. MCP is in wide use today. WebMCP is still a draft, in trial in Chrome, and not yet available to every user.

MCP: a standard plug for AI

Before MCP, every connection between an assistant and a system was built by hand. MCP, introduced by Anthropic in November 2024, defines one way to describe a tool: what it does, what it needs and what it returns. A business that publishes an MCP server lets compatible assistants look up its services or availability directly.

WebMCP: tools inside the page

With WebMCP the page itself tells the agent what it can do there, for example "search products" or "request a quote", instead of the agent guessing from buttons and forms. As of late 2026 it is a draft from a W3C community group. Chrome offers it through a trial, and the way a page declares its tools changed during 2026, so early tutorials are already out of date.

What should a business do now?

First make the site readable: complete HTML, clear pages, structured data.

Publish an MCP server if customers or partners already use assistants that support it.

Add WebMCP tools as an experiment, and expect to update them as the draft changes.

Decide which actions an agent may take alone and which need a person to approve.

---

# How to prepare your website for AI agents

URL: https://www.vargersoft.com/resources/how-to-prepare-your-website-for-ai-agents/

To prepare a website for AI agents, make every page readable without running scripts, state your services, prices, hours and location in plain text, add structured data, allow AI crawlers in robots.txt, and give agents a clear way to act, such as a simple form or an MCP server. Most of this is the same work that helps search engines and people.

Step 1: check what a machine sees

Open a page, choose "View page source" and search for a sentence you can read on screen. If it is missing, the content is added later by scripts, and many crawlers will never see it.

Step 2: say the facts in text

Agents compare businesses on facts: what you do, where, when, and for how much. Put them in sentences and tables. A price that only appears inside an image does not exist for a machine.

Step 3: add structured data

Structured data is a labeled copy of the same facts in a format machines read without guessing: this is the business name, this is a service, this is its price. It is invisible to visitors and useful to every crawler.

Step 4: open the door

Check robots.txt. If it blocks AI crawlers, assistants cannot use your pages in their answers. Allow the ones you want and keep a sitemap that lists every page.

Step 5: make the action simple

An agent that wants to book or ask for a quote needs a short path: a form with clear labels, or tools published through an MCP server. Decide which requests can be confirmed automatically and which a person approves.

---

# What should a small business automate first?

URL: https://www.vargersoft.com/resources/what-to-automate-first-in-a-small-business/

Automate first the task that is repeated every day, follows the same steps each time and costs you customers when it is done late. For most small businesses that is answering the phone, following up on quotes or confirming appointments. Fix the process before you automate it, because automating a broken process only makes it fail faster.

Three questions to find the task

Does it happen at least once a day?

Could you write its steps on one page?

Does a customer wait, or leave, when it is late?

A task with three yes answers is a good first candidate. A task that needs judgment every time is not.

Fix it on paper first

Write the steps as they really happen, not as they should. Remove the ones nobody needs. Decide what the right result looks like. Only then choose a tool.

Set one number and one date

Before you start, pick the number the automation should move, such as missed calls per week or days to collect an invoice, and the date you will check it. If the number has not moved by that date, change the plan.

What to leave alone

Keep people on the moments that build trust: a complaint, a negotiation, bad news. Automation should carry the routine so your team has time for those.

# About VARGERSOFT

URL: https://www.vargersoft.com/about/

We built the software we could not buy

For years we bought business software for our own companies, and for years we ended up running the business from a spreadsheet next to it. Then we noticed the same spreadsheet on every other owner's desk: hardware, parts, transportation, manufacturing. Small and mid-size businesses are sold enterprise software with features removed and the price barely reduced. VARGERSOFT exists to close that gap.

Anyone can write code now. Knowing what to build is the hard part.

AI made software cheap to produce. It did not make it easier to know which step of a process is actually costing the money. That takes having signed the payroll, chased the missing part and closed a month that did not add up. We use AI as a tool and bring the operating judgment ourselves.

Where the experience comes from

VARGER Group LLC was formed in Texas in 2026. The team behind it has engineered processes and run operating businesses since 2002: eight years in automotive quality engineering on OEM programs for GM, Ford, Volvo, Nissan and Stellantis, and more than fifteen years building and running retail, manufacturing and service companies.
